drift: D1.5 from individual strict majority estimand to clustered aggregation estimand in sociological evaluation

A.question: Does session_bootstrap_ci estimate the mean of sessions or the mean of recorded observations when session sizes differ, and can a separate block bootstrap target the latter without treating individual rows as independent?
A.population: Synthetic clusters of parliamentary sessions with unequal observed rollcall sample sizes

estimands.session_equal: Average of session-specific means, each session one unit
estimands.record_equal: Sum of observed values divided by count of observed records, each row one unit; uncertainty clustered by session

A.primary_comparison: 100 zeros in session A; one ten in B: session equal mean=5, record equal mean=10/101

B.H1: Existing session_bootstrap_ci is session-equal; calling it an observation mean would introduce weighting bias under unequal cluster sizes
B.H0: Existing outputs are already observation-weighted in both point estimate and resamples
B.alternative: Both estimands scientifically legitimate when explicitly specified; difference is not code failure absent contract

controls: Maintain full-session block resampling for uncertainty, no per-vote i.i.d bootstrap
